title: The Dark Vienna
description: Take your Vienna knowledge to the next level with this BONUS mini course. This pairs well with the 1.e4 Gotham Style Part 1.

r1b1r1k1/ppp2pp1/2np1q1p/8/1b2P3/2NQ4/PP.text:
When Black recaptures...

We can jump our knight to d5, hitting Black's queen, bishop and the c7-pawn.

r1b2rk1/ppp1qppp/3p1n2/1Q2n3/4P3/P1B2P2/.text:
And we'll go f3, supporting e4.

Black will likely challenge our queen and we'll bring it back to e2.

After that, we can look to start a pawn storm!

r1b2rk1/ppp1qppp/3p1n2/1Q2n3/4P3/P1B5/1P.text: Black goes ...d6, defending their knight and opening up their bishop.

r1b2rk1/ppppqppp/5n2/1Q2n3/1b2P3/2N5/PPP.text:
A better way to deal with the double attack is ...Qe7, defending both the bishop and the knight.

Against this, we should push a3, simply attacking Black's bishop.

r1b2rk1/ppppqppp/5n2/1Q2n3/4P3/P1b5/1PPB.text:
There are no good squares for the bishop, so Black is forced to take our knight and give up the bishop pair.

We'll recapture with the bishop.

r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/8/1b2P3/2NQ4/PPP.text:
Black can also play the natural ...d6, opening up the light-squared bishop.

This is played 30% of the time.

Since we don't need to play f3, we should use this moment to go Qg3.

r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2np4/2b4n/4P3/2N1Q3/PPP.text: And if Black brings their bishop back and attacks our queen once more...

r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2np4/2b4n/4P3/2N5/PPPB1.text:
We can simply bring the queen back.

Our plan is unaltered - pawn storm!

r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2np4/7n/1b2P3/2N3Q1/PPP.text:
Black can also go ...Nh5, attacking our queen and forcing it to move away from the active g3-square.

Against this, we'll go Qe3, and the plan here is pretty standard. 

We want to push on the kingside.

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/1b2P3/2NQ4/PPP.text:
Black proceeds by castling kingside.

We'll respond by castling queenside.

This essentially means that we should try to attack Black on the kingside, and Black should try to attack us on the queenside.

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/4P3/2BQ4/PPP2P.text:
Black proceeds by castling kingside.

We'll respond by castling queenside, which is more natural in this case.

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/5n2/1Q2n3/4P3/2b5/PPPB.text:
The most common and natural response is to simply take on c3.

This, however, isn't good. Not only is Black giving us the bishop pair, but also improving the placement of our dark-squared bishop.

We should recapture with our bishop.

If Black now opts to retreat the knight to either c6 or g6, we'll proceed with f3, supporting e4, and then follow it up with the typical pawn storm.

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/5n2/1Q6/4P1n1/2B5/PPP2.text: And if Black keeps trying to pose problems by threatening ...Nxf2...

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/5n2/4n3/1b2P3/2NQ4/PPP.text:
Black can also get confrontational and attack our queen with ...Ne5.

This is the least common of the three options and has been played in only about 7% of games, but it's important to know how to best deal with it.

We'll respond with Qb5, double attacking Black's bishop and knight.

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/4P1n1/2B5/PPP1QP.text:
We can simply bring our queen back and defend against Black's threat.

White is much better as Black has made a lot of superficial threats and has only managed to improve our position. 

We'll go f3 to kick back the knight and support the e4-pawn, and follow up with the pawn storm on the kingside.

r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/1b2P3/2NQ4/PPP2.text:
By far the most popular continuation is ...Bb4, developing the dark-squared bishop and pinning our knight.

This move is played half the time.

We'll respond by developing our dark-squared bishop and breaking the pin.

r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/4P3/2bQ4/PPPB1P.text:
Played 10% of the time is ...Bxc3.

This really isn't great. Black is giving up the bishop pair unprovoked and improving our dark-squared bishop.

We'll recapture with our bishop.

r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/3QP3/2N5/PPP2P.text:
Black proceeds by developing their knight and attacking our queen.

And we'll respond by sliding our queen back one square.

We did waste a bit of time with our queen, but the center has opened up and we have an active plan: develop the dark-squared bishop, castle queenside and develop an attack.

r1bqr1k1/1pp2pp1/3p3p/p1n5/4P3/P4P2/1PPQ.text:
Black improves their knight.

We'll proceed with Nd4, centralizing the knight and opening up our bishop.

r1bqr1k1/1pp2pp1/3p3p/p7/1n2P3/8/PPPQNPP.text:
Black supports the knight by advancing their a-pawn.

We'll kick Black's knight back.

r1bqr1k1/1pp2pp1/n2p3p/p7/4P3/P7/1PPQNPP.text:
Black goes back to a6, looking to route the knight to the c5-square.

We'll go f3, supporting the e4-pawn.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2pp1/2np1n1p/6B1/1b2P3/2NQ4/.text:
Most logical is ...h6, simply attacking the bishop and forcing a decision.

We'll capture Black's knight.

We do this because we have a concrete followup.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2pp1/2np3p/3N4/1b2P3/3Q4/PPP.text:
Black is forced to move the queen all the way back to d8 to defend c7.

Now we can capture the bishop.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2pp1/3p3p/8/1n2P3/3Q4/PPP1NP.text:
And when Black recaptures...

We can simply move the queen back a square, attacking Black's knight.

...Nxa2+ isn't an issue as it would result in the knight getting trapped.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/8/1b2P3/2N3Q1/PP.text:
Black brings the rook to the open file where it exerts pressure against e4.

We'll go f3, supporting the e4-pawn.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/8/1b2P3/2NQ4/PPP.text:
Usually, Black proceeds with ...d6, opening up the light-squared bishop.

This is played 58% of the time.

Our bishop has done it's job on d2 so we'll move it to g5, pinning the knight.

This pin needs to be addressed immediately because Nd5 is a threat.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/8/4P3/2BQ1P2/PPP.text:
Black proceeds naturally with ...d6, opening up the light-squared bishop.

We'll develop our knight to e2, with the idea to bring it to the f4-square.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2ppp/3p1n2/4n1B1/1b2P3/2NQ4/.text:
Black can also go ...Ne5, attacking our queen, but this is quite bad.

We'll simply move our queen to g3.

We are now threatening two things: Nd5, and f4, followed by e5.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2ppp/3p1nn1/6B1/1b2P2P/2N3Q1.text:
But now we advance the h-pawn.

White has a decisive attack on the kingside. With h5 and Nd5 on the way, Black's position is bound to collapse.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2ppp/3p1nn1/6B1/1b2P3/2N3Q1/.text: Black can try to move out of the way by bringing the knight back to g6...

r1bqr1k1/ppp2ppp/3p4/4Q1Bn/1b2P3/2N5/PPP.text:
Qxe5 is the cold shower and Black has no way to avoid losing material.

White is completely winning here.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2ppp/3p4/4n1Bn/1b2P3/2N3Q1/P.text: Attempting to defend tactically with ...Nh5 immediately loses for Black.

r1bqr1k1/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/1b2P3/2NQ4/PPP.text:
Played 50% of the time is the natural ...Re8, bringing the rook to the open file and putting some pressure on e4.

We should proceed with Nge2.

The simple point is to add some more support to the c3-knight, but also not to block the advance of the f-pawn.

r1bqr1k1/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/4P3/2BQ4/PPP2P.text:
Black then goes ...Re8, bringing the rook to the open file and attacking e4.

We'll go f3, supporting the e4-pawn.

r1bqr1k1/pppp1ppp/5n2/4n3/1b2P3/2NQ4/PPP.text:
Black might also try to get aggressive with ...Ne5, attacking our queen. This is played 27% of the time.

Against this, we'll go for Qg3.

If Black plays slowly now, we'll go Bg5 and look to attack on the kingside...

r1bqr1k1/pppp1ppp/8/4n2n/1b2P3/2N3Q1/PPP.text:
That's why Black really should attack the queen once again with ...Nh5.

And we should move our queen to e3.

If Black now decides to stop being confrontational, we'll look to proceed with Ng3 and f4 at the right moment.

r1bqr1k1/pppp1ppp/8/7n/1Q2P3/2N5/PPP1NPP.text:
And we'll recapture with the h-rook.

White is better. We have more space and our pieces are more active.

The plan here is simple - pawnstorm!
The knight has no way out, so Black is forced to capture the f1-bishop.

r1bqr1k1/pppp1ppp/8/7n/1b1QP3/2N5/PPPnNP.text:
And when Black takes our bishop...

We'll take Black's bishop.

r1bqr1k1/pppp1ppp/8/7n/1bn1P3/2N1Q3/PPPB.text:
And if Black insists on confrontation by attacking our queen again...

We should respond with Qd4.

r2qr1k1/1pp2ppp/p1npbn2/8/4P3/P1BQ1P2/1P.text:
Black goes ...a6, controlling b5 and supporting a future b-pawn advance.

We'll continue by improving the placement of our knight.

r2qr1k1/1pp2ppp/p2pbn2/4n3/4PN2/P1B1QP2/.text:
But we can simply respond by moving our queen over one square.

White is much better here. We have more space and better pieces.

The immediate threat is Bxe5 to win a piece, and our plan in this position is to develop our light-squared bishop and follow up with a pawn storm.

r2qr1k1/1pp2ppp/p2pbn2/4n3/4PN2/P1BQ1P2/.text: Black might then centralize their knight and attack our queen.

r2qr1k1/1ppb1pp1/3p3p/p1n5/3NP1P1/P4P2/1.text:
And now we'll push g4, beginning the attacking operations on the kingside!

The engine might only give a slight edge to White, but this position isn't fun to play as Black. The kingside attack is quickly coming and one inaccurate move can lose the game.

Our approach kicked Black's pieces back and ensured we have a strong center, as well. Our plan is to develop the bishop and pawn storm on the kingside.

r2qr1k1/1ppb1pp1/3p3p/p1n5/3NP3/P4P2/1PP.text: Black's most logical is ...Bd7, simply developing the light-squared bishop.

r2qr1k1/ppp2p1p/2nbb1p1/2P5/5P1P/2B3Q1/P.text:
We go c5, winning the d6-bishop!

After this forced line and a sharp combination, we are winning.

Good game.

r2qr1k1/ppp2ppp/2n1b3/3n4/1b5P/2N2PQ1/PP.text:
Black recaptures with their knight.

We'll then capture Black's knight.

r2qr1k1/ppp2ppp/2n1bn2/3p4/1b2P2P/2N2PQ1.text:
And a pretty logical thing to do is to break in the center with ...d5.

This, however, runs into trouble.

We'll capture with our e-pawn.

r2qr1k1/ppp2ppp/2n5/3b4/1b5P/5PQ1/PPPB2P.text:
And when Black recaptures...

We can advance with c4, attacking the bishop that's pinned along the d-file!

Black is losing a piece here.

r2qr1k1/ppp2ppp/2nb4/3b4/2P4P/5PQ1/PP1B2.text:
The only way to try to save a piece is ...Bd6, but this doesn't quite work...

We should respond by advancing f4 and blocking the attack on our queen.

r2qr1k1/ppp2ppp/2nbb3/8/2P2P1P/6Q1/PP1B2.text:
And when Black moves their bishop...

We can go Bc3, threatening mate.

r2qr1k1/ppp2ppp/2npbn2/8/1b2P3/2N2PQ1/PP.text:
Black proceeds naturally by developing their final minor piece.

And now we begin a kingside attack by advancing our h-pawn!

We're threatening to advance h5 and h6, so Black needs to do something...

r2qr1k1/ppp2ppp/2npbn2/8/4P3/2BQ1P2/PPP1.text:
Black proceeds by developing their final minor piece to an active square.

I suggest we proceed with a3, making sure there's never any ...Bxa2 ideas.

rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/4p3/4P3/2N5/PPPP1P.text:
This chapter will cover the move 2...Nf6, which is played roughly a third of the time.

We strike in the center with d4!

This unconventional pawn advance is the essence of the Dark Vienna. 

The idea is to open up the center and get dynamic middlegame positions filled with tactics and attacking ideas.

rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/3pP3/2N5/PPP2PPP.text:
This study will deal with the most popular and natural response for Black, which is capturing on d4, and it's played 65% of the time.

Black simply wants to force our queen out and use it as a target.

We should, of course, recapture. 

Our queen can be targeted here, but that doesn't bother us all that much.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
Black responds with 1...e5.

Instead of proceeding in the most standard way with 2. Nf3, we will develop the queenside knight to c3.

This move characterizes the Vienna.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
Welcome to this course about a completely new, exciting way of playing the Vienna with White!

If you enjoy attacking and want to take your opponents out of their comfort zone as early as move three, you have come to the right place.

This first study will deal with Black capturing our pawn on d4 after we advance in the center.

r1bq1rk1/ppp2p2/1bnp1n1p/6p1/4P2B/2N2N2/.text:
Black decides to advance ...g5.

Now we sacrifice the knight!

r1bq1rk1/ppp2p2/1bnp1n2/6B1/4P3/2N5/PPP1.text:
And we capture the g5-pawn with our bishop, renewing the powerful pin.

Black is in serious trouble here. 

Nd5 is coming, the king is wide open and our queen and rook can quickly join the attack.

r1bq1rk1/ppp2pp1/1bnp1n1p/6B1/4P3/2N2N2/.text:
The way to do so is ...h6, attacking the bishop and forcing a decision.

We'll slide the bishop back a square, maintaining the pin and posing Black a serious question: 

Can they go ...g5?

r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/1bnp1n2/8/4PB2/2N2N2/PP.text:
Black retreats the bishop to safety.

We go Bg5, pinning the knight and looking to follow up with Nd5.

Allowing Nd5 is not a good idea for Black, so they need to deal with the pin immediately...

r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/2b5/4PB2/2NQ4/PP.text:
Black can also proceed in a more calm manner with ...d6, simply opening up the light-squared bishop.

We can now go f3, supporting e4 and preparing a future g-pawn advance.

r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/8/4PB2/2NQ1N2/PP.text:
Black castles their king.

And now it's important that we go Qe2, attacking Black's bishop.

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b5/4PB2/2NQ4/PP.text:
Black proceeds by castling kingside.

We'll respond by castling queenside.

This is where things get spicy as we are sacrificing the f2-pawn.

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/4PB2/2NQ4/PPP2.text:
Black decides to call our bluff and captures the free pawn on f2.

Now we'll advance our e-pawn and attack Black's knight, forcing it to move to an awkward square.

If Black now opts for ...Ne8 or ...Ng4, we can proceed with Nf3 and more than sufficient compensation for the pawn.

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/2b5/4PB2/2NQ3N/PPP.text:
Black captures f2 with their knight.

We capture Black's knight.

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/2b5/4PBn1/2NQ4/PPP.text:
Black can also go ...Ng4, looking to capture the f2-pawn with the knight.

We have to stop ...Nxf2 from coming with a fork, so we play Nh3, adding a defender to the f2-pawn.

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P2n/5B2/2NQ4/PPP2.text:
And if Black chooses to go ...Nh5, attacking our dark-squared bishop...

We can simply slide the bishop back.

This position is already quite difficult for Black. We have compensation for the pawn and Qf3 is a serious threat.

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/2n5/8/4PB2/2NQ4/PPP2bP.text:
Black recaptures.

And now we can advance e5, taking some space and opening up our queen's vision towards the kingside.

r1bq1rk1/pppp1ppp/8/4nQ1n/8/2N5/PPPB1bPP.text:
We win material with Qf5, triple attacking Black's minor pieces!

This is just a sample of how easily you can be winning if Black doesn't respect your Dark Vienna setup!

r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/2b5/4PB2/2NQ4/PPP.text:
Black can also proceed with ...d6, opening up the light-squared bishop.

We'll respond by castling queenside.

Once again, we're gambiting a pawn.

r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/8/4PB2/2NQ4/PPP2b.text:
Black captures the f2-pawn.

We proceed by developing our knight.

Development is more essential than material here.

r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b5/4P3/2NQ4/PPP2.text:
Black's second option is to develop the dark-squared bishop to c5.

This is played 15% of the time and the idea is to quickly target the f2-pawn.

Against this, we'll develop our dark-squared bishop to f4 and prepare queenside castling.

r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/3QP3/2N5/PPP2P.text:
Black proceeds by developing their knight and attacking our queen.

And we'll respond by sliding our queen back one square.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2p2/1bnp1n1p/3N2p1/4P2B/5N2/.text:
Black must now go ...g5 in order to break the pin on their knight.

We'll respond by sacrificing the knight.

Capturing the knight isn't a good idea (as we've seen in the line where Black advances ...g5 immediately)...

r1bqr1k1/ppp2p2/1bnp3p/3R2N1/4P2B/8/PPP1.text:
And we recapture with the rook.

The engine finds a way to hold equality here (with ...Qf6), but the position is far from easy to play for Black.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2pp1/1bnp1n1p/8/4P2B/2N2N2/P.text:
Black can also refuse to break the pin immediately and go ...Re8 instead.

Now we'll go Nd5, putting some pressure on the pinned f6-knight.

r1bqr1k1/pppp1p1p/1bn3p1/4P1N1/5B2/3Q4/P.text:
Black has to defend with ...g6.

Now we swing our queen over to the h-file, threatening Qxh7+ again.

r1bqr1k1/pppp1p2/1bn3p1/4P1Np/5B2/6Q1/PP.text:
And now we go Qg3, supporting the e5-pawn and sidestepping any discoveries from Black's c8-bishop.

Black is simply defenseless here.

r1bqr1k1/pppp1p2/1bn3p1/4P1Np/5B2/7Q/PPP.text: The only way to defend against the threat of Qxh7+ is to advance ...h5.

r1bqr1k1/pppp1ppp/1bn5/4P3/4NB2/3Q4/PPP3.text:
And when Black saves their bishop...

We go Ng5, threatening Qxh7+!

r1bqr1k1/pppp1ppp/2n5/4P3/5B2/2NQ4/PPP2b.text:
If Black now attacks the e5-pawn...

We have the strong response Ne4, attacking Black's bishop on f2.

r2q1rk1/1pp2ppp/p1npbn2/2b5/4PB2/2N2P2/P.text:
A logical way to proceed is ...a6, preparing to advance the b-pawn.

We'll improve our king's placement.

r2q1rk1/2p2ppp/p1npbn2/1pb5/4PB2/2N2P2/P.text:
Black follows up with ...b5, launching an attack on the queenside.

We'll respond with h4, launching our own attack on the opposite side.

r2q1rk1/2p2ppp/p1npbn2/2b5/1p2PB1P/2N2P2.text:
Black advances the b-pawn once more and attacks our knight.

We should respond Na4, eyeing Black's dark-squared bishop.

r2q1rk1/b1p2pp1/p1npbn1p/7P/Np2PB2/5P2/P.text: And when Black stops our h-pawn...

r2q1rk1/b1p2pp1/p1npbn1p/7P/Np2PBP1/5P2/.text:
Here comes the reinforcement! 

We are threatening to rip apart the kingside with g5 and Black has to defend very accurately.

Practically speaking, White definitely has an edge with the kingside attack.

r2q1rk1/b1p2ppp/p1npbn2/8/Np2PB1P/5P2/PP.text:
Black doesn't want to lose their strong bishop, so they retreat it.

We keep advancing our h-pawn.

r2q1rk1/ppp2ppp/2npbn2/2b5/4PB2/2NQ1P2/P.text:
Black develops the light-squared bishop to the most active square.

Now I suggest we go Qd2 in order to sidestep any ...Nb4 or ...Ne5 ideas.

rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/4p3/4P3/2N5/PPPP1P.text:
This chapter will cover the move 2...Nf6.

We strike in the center with d4!

rnbqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/3pP3/2N5/PPP2PPP.text:
Black takes on d4.

We should, of course, recapture.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
Black responds with 1...e5.

Instead of proceeding in the most standard way with 2. Nf3, we will develop the queenside knight to c3.

This move characterizes the Vienna.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
For this second study, we'll analyze what to play after 3...exd4 and bishop to c5 on move 5. 

The bishop on c5 doesn't pin the knight, but it targets our pawn on f2. This isn't a major problem and we can get a good position afterwards.

r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/8/4PB2/2NQ4/PPP.text:
Black castles kingside.

Now we go f3, supporting e4 and preparing a future g-pawn advance.

r1bqk2r/ppp1bppp/2np1n2/8/4PB2/2NQ4/PPP2.text:
Black's most natural way to proceed is ...Be7, preparing ...O-O.

We'll castle queenside.

r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/2np1n2/8/4P3/2NQ4/PPP2P.text:
Third in popularity is ...d6, simply opening up the light-squared bishop.

This is played about 13% of the time.

Against ...d6, we will develop our dark-squared bishop to f4 and prepare queenside castling.

r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/3p1n2/8/1n2P3/2N5/PPP1Q.text:
Black's most logical way to continue is ...d6, opening up the light-squared bishop and covering the e5-square.

Now we develop our dark-squared bishop to f4, preparing O-O-O.

r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/8/3QP3/2N5/PPP2P.text:
Black proceeds by developing their knight and attacking our queen.

We'll slide back to d3.

r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/5n2/8/1n2P3/2NQ4/PPP2P.text:
Black's fourth and final option is the confrontational ...Nb4, attacking our queen, eyeing the c2-pawn and looking to advance the d-pawn.

This is played roughly 7% of the time.

The best response is Qe2. We save our queen, guard c2 and stop ...d5.

r2q1rk1/1pp1bppp/p1npbn2/8/4PB2/2NQ1P2/P.text:
A logical way to proceed is ...a6, preparing to advance the b-pawn.

But ...b5 doesn't worry us, as we can proceed by developing the g1-knight.

r2q1rk1/2p1bppp/p1npbn2/1p6/4PB2/2NQ1P2/.text:
